title: Program wire — client effect (§5.2)
description: The rendering surface's closed vocabulary, and the specification's ONE enumerated envelope exception: the discriminator member is `kind`, not `$type`, and the emitted member order is declaration order rather than Ordinal. A JSON Schema cannot express member ORDER at all, which is exactly why the corpus rather than this file is what pins the exception — see client-effect/download.json, where `url` precedes `name`.

navigate.description: `target` is optional and closed. It is OMITTED at its identity `Self`, so `"Blank"` is the only value that appears on this wire; a schema cannot express omit-at-default, which is why §5.2 states it and the corpus pins it with client-effect/navigate.json beside client-effect/navigate-target.json.

print.description: Format version 2. The payload-free arm: `kind` and nothing else. The emptiness is normative — the paged medium belongs to the host and every parameter of the printing to the reader's own dialogue — so `additionalProperties: false` over a single declared member is the whole shape, and a document carrying anything beside `kind` is refused as `undeclared-member`.

confirm.description: Format version 2. `prompt` is the question; `token` names WHICH confirmation in the originating gesture is being answered. Both required. What a yes will DO is deliberately absent — the continuations stay with whoever holds the tree, the gate and the egress policy — and the answer returns on the ORIGINATING event re-delivered with `confirmToken` / `confirmAccepted`, which is a payload shape on another wire and therefore not expressible here. §5.2 states both, and a schema that could express neither is why the text governs and this file is subordinate to it.
